FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A131
Line color answers which way traffic flows, yellow for opposite directions and white for the same direction, before line style answers whether you may cross. [A131]
Why it matters: group_hint line-color; prereq_hint sec10-F01; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec10-F04.
Source: [A131 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A132
Dashed white permits a safe lane change, single solid white asks you to stay put except in a special situation, and double solid white makes crossing illegal. [A132]
Why it matters: group_hint white-lines; prereq_hint sec10-R01; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec10-F07, sec10-F08, sec10-F09.
Source: [A132 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A131
Ordinary dashed white lines can be crossed when safe, but the shorter dashed white lines warn that your own lane is about to end. [A131]
Why it matters: group_hint white-lines; prereq_hint sec10-R02; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec10-F05, sec10-F07.
Source: [A131 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A132
A dashed yellow centerline allows passing when safe, while a single solid yellow line or double solid yellow lines forbid passing. [A132]
Why it matters: group_hint yellow-lines; prereq_hint sec10-R01; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec10-F10, sec10-F11, sec10-F12.
Source: [A132 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A133
With one solid and one dashed yellow line, the line on your own side decides: solid means no passing for you, dashed means you may pass when safe. [A133]
Why it matters: group_hint yellow-lines; prereq_hint sec10-R04; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec10-F13.
Source: [A133 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A133
A solid yellow line on your side bans passing, but you may still cross it to enter a center lane marked with left turn arrows. [A133]
Why it matters: group_hint center-lane; prereq_hint sec10-R04; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec10-F13, sec10-F15.
Source: [A133 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A134
A shared center lane is for turning, never for passing, and you should not stay in it longer than 300 feet. [A134]
Why it matters: group_hint center-lane; prereq_hint sec10-R06; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec10-F16, sec10-F17.
Source: [A134 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A135
Reversible lanes are usually marked with double-dashed white lines, but the overhead signals, not the paint, tell you whether you may use the lane right now. [A135]
Why it matters: group_hint special-lanes; prereq_hint sec10-F20; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec10-F21, sec10-F22.
Source: [A135 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A135
A red X over a reversible lane bars you from it, while a steady yellow X means the lane is switching direction and you should get out of it soon and safely. [A135]
Why it matters: group_hint special-lanes; prereq_hint sec10-F20; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec10-F22.
Source: [A135 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A136
In an express or high occupancy toll lane the toll is only for drivers who do not qualify for the free ride that buses, vanpools, carpools and motorcycles get. [A136]
Why it matters: group_hint special-lanes; prereq_hint sec10-F18; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec10-F19, sec10-F24.
Source: [A136 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A138
A fire lane forbids stopping as well as parking, and some communities paint one on the road in front of a fire station, not only along a red curb. [A138]
Why it matters: group_hint other-markings; prereq_hint sec10-F01; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec10-F32, sec10-F33.
Source: [A138 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A140
The 20 mph school zone limit covers the roads near a school building or playground, and posted signs may clarify the times when it applies. [A140]
Why it matters: group_hint zones; prereq_hint sec10-F36; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec10-F36.
Source: [A140 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0140]
